name: Java - Spring Boot
scope: A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in Java - Spring Boot as a competency should be able to design, build, and optimize complex Spring Boot applications using core Java (OOP, generics, streams, concurrency, memory management), apply SOLID and clean code principles, and manage builds with Maven/Gradle. They deeply understand Spring Core (bean lifecycle, DI, scopes, proxies, autoconfiguration, profiles, configuration properties), can structure RESTful APIs with Spring MVC/WebFlux, handle error/exception mapping, validation, and advanced serialization (Jackson), and implement both servlet and reactive stacks. They are skilled in Spring Data JPA (entity mapping, repositories, transactions, multi-DB, migrations with Flyway/Liquibase), and can integrate alternative stores (MongoDB, Redis), ensuring data integrity and consistency. They configure and customize Spring Security (auth, authz, JWT, OAuth2/OIDC, CSRF, CORS, secure endpoints, custom providers), mitigate vulnerabilities, and apply secure-by-default practices. They integrate with external systems using RestTemplate/WebClient, messaging (Kafka, RabbitMQ, JMS, Spring Integration/Cloud Stream), implement async processing (@Async, @Scheduled), and design for resilience (circuit breakers, retries, bulkheads). They architect microservices with Spring Boot, apply layered/hexagonal/DDD patterns, use Spring Cloud (discovery, config, load balancing), and balance standardization with flexibility. They optimize for performance, scalability, and reliability (profiling, tuning pools, GC, stateless design, backpressure, rate limiting, graceful degradation), and implement comprehensive testing (unit, slice, integration, contract, MockMvc, TestRestTemplate, testcontainers, CI/CD integration). They use Spring Boot Actuator, Micrometer, and distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, Zipkin, Jaeger), configure structured logging (MDC, correlation IDs), and interpret observability data for improvements. They package, containerize (Docker), and deploy to cloud/Kubernetes, manage environment-specific configs, secrets, and runtime hooks, and collaborate on incident response. They manage dependencies, automate builds, integrate code quality/security tools, and standardize templates. They lead code reviews, mentor peers, collaborate across roles, contribute to shared libraries/standards, and participate in post-mortems. They document APIs (OpenAPI), configs, and architecture, align docs with code, support governance and compliance, and drive knowledge sharing and organizational standards for Spring Boot.

{"sections":[{"name":"Core Java & Spring Fundamentals (Expected Solid Mastery)","scope_included":"- Demonstrate strong command of core Java language features as they are applied in Spring Boot services:
  - Object-oriented design principles (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, composition)
  - Interfaces, abstract classes, inner classes, anonymous classes
  - Generics, collections, streams, functional interfaces, lambda expressions, method references
  - Exception hierarchy, checked vs unchecked exceptions, custom exceptions, exception propagation
  - Concurrency primitives (threads, locks, synchronized), plus high-level concurrency APIs (ExecutorService, CompletableFuture) where relevant to Spring-based async workflows
  - Immutability, value objects, and proper equals/hashCode/toString implementations
- Apply SOLID principles and clean code practices when designing Spring Boot components (controllers, services, repositories, configuration classes)
- Understand and apply Java memory model concepts in the context of long-running Spring Boot services:
  - Heap vs stack, garbage collection impact on service performance
  - Object lifecycle and memory leaks common in Spring applications (e.g., misused static references, caches)
- Use Java build and dependency management effectively for Spring Boot:
  - Mature usage of Maven or Gradle (multi-module projects, dependency scopes, BOMs, version alignment)
  - Manage transitive dependencies and resolve conflicts that impact Spring Boot autoconfiguration or runtime behavior
- Understand how Java versions impact Spring Boot (language features, module system, supported versions, JVM flags relevant for production Spring apps)
- Read and reason about JDK and external API documentation to integrate Java libraries cleanly with Spring Boot applications","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Spring Core & Dependency Injection","scope_included":"- Have deep understanding of Spring Core container and how it underpins Spring Boot:
  - Bean lifecycle (instantiation, dependency injection, initialization, destruction)
  - Bean scopes (singleton, prototype, request, session, application, custom scopes) and when to use each
  - Bean post-processors, BeanFactoryPostProcessor, BeanPostProcessor, and their impact on application behavior
  - Aware of circular dependency issues, root causes, detection, and resolution strategies
- Design robust dependency injection structures:
  - Use constructor injection as the primary pattern, understanding trade-offs with field and setter injection
  - Manage optional dependencies and lazy initialization where appropriate
  - Recognize and refactor over-wired classes and God-services
- Use and understand configuration mechanisms:
  - Java-based configuration (@Configuration, @Bean, @Import, @Profile)
  - Conditional configuration (@Conditional, @ConditionalOn* variants used by Spring Boot autoconfiguration)
  - Profile-based configuration and environment-specific wiring
- Understand how component scanning works:
  - Base packages, include/exclude filters, and their effect on startup and structure
  - Avoid ambiguous bean definitions, name clashes, and unintended component scanning
- Use and customize Spring Boot autoconfiguration:
  - Understand how autoconfiguration classes are loaded and can be enabled/disabled
  - Know how to override autoconfigured beans cleanly without breaking future upgrades
  - Configure custom starters or assemble internal starters for company-wide standards
- Understand proxying mechanisms used by Spring:
  - JDK dynamic proxies vs CGLIB proxies
  - Impact on AOP, transactional methods, and self-invocation limitations
  - Recognize situations where proxies will not apply and how to restructure code","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Spring Boot Core Concepts & Application Lifecycle","scope_included":"- Understand Spring Boot application lifecycle end-to-end:
  - Application startup sequence: classpath scanning, environment preparation, context creation, autoconfiguration, runners (CommandLineRunner, ApplicationRunner)
  - Shutdown hooks, graceful shutdown, and lifecycle callbacks
- Design and structure Spring Boot applications for maintainability:
  - Modularization within a single codebase (packages, modules, feature-based organization)
  - Breaking monoliths into independently deployable Spring Boot services when appropriate
- Master application configuration management:
  - Properties vs YAML configuration, property binding (@ConfigurationProperties, @Value)
  - Externalized configuration sources (environment variables, command-line args, config files, config server, Vault/secret stores)
  - Hierarchy and precedence of Spring Boot property sources
  - Complex type binding (lists, maps, nested objects) and validation of configuration
- Customize Spring Boot behavior:
  - Banner, logging system, application environment, embedded server configuration
  - Customizing SpringApplication and SpringApplicationBuilder
  - Profiles, groups of profiles, and profile-specific beans and properties
- Use Spring Boot starters effectively:
  - Understand purpose of major starters (web, data, security, actuator, validation, batch, integration, messaging, cloud)
  - Avoid unnecessary starters and manage bloat, startup time, and attack surface
- Manage version alignment and upgrades:
  - Understand Spring Boot’s dependency management and alignment of Spring ecosystem versions
  - Plan and execute upgrades between Spring Boot minor/major versions, handling deprecations and behavior changes","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"RESTful APIs, Web Layer & Reactive Programming","scope_included":"- Build robust REST APIs with Spring MVC:
  - Design controllers with clear separation of concerns (controllers vs services vs repositories)
  - Use @RestController, @Controller, @RequestMapping and composed annotations for HTTP methods
  - Handle path variables, query params, headers, cookies, and matrix variables when needed
  - Support content negotiation, versioning strategies, and error handling conventions
- Implement comprehensive error and exception handling:
  - Use @ControllerAdvice, @ExceptionHandler, ResponseStatusException, and consistent error response models
  - Map validation, business, and infrastructure errors to appropriate HTTP status codes
- Work with serialization and JSON processing:
  - Configure Jackson (or alternative mappers) globally and per-property
  - Handle nulls, dates, time zones, enums, polymorphism, and custom serializers/deserializers
  - Prevent serialization issues (lazy-loaded JPA relations, bidirectional references, large graphs)
- Implement request/response validation:
  - Use Bean Validation (JSR 380) with @Valid, @Validated, constraint annotations, and custom validators
  - Design DTOs for API boundaries and map them to domain models cleanly
- Understand servlet vs reactive stacks and choose appropriately:
  - Know capabilities and trade-offs between Spring MVC (Tomcat/Jetty/Undertow) and Spring WebFlux (Netty)
  - Understand when reactive programming is beneficial (high concurrency IO-bound, backpressure requirements)
- Use reactive programming with Spring WebFlux at a working level:
  - Build simple reactive endpoints with Mono/Flux
  - Understand basic operators, backpressure concepts, and Reactor types
  - Integrate reactive repositories (e.g., R2DBC, reactive Mongo) where appropriate, or explain constraints in a legacy environment
- Implement cross-cutting web concerns:
  - Filters, interceptors, argument resolvers
  - Global and per-endpoint CORS configuration
  - Rate-limiting strategies at the web layer (header-based, IP-based, token-bucket mechanisms), even if implemented via external components/gateways","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Data Persistence & Transaction Management","scope_included":"- Use Spring Data JPA effectively:
  - Entity mapping, relationships, cascade types, fetch types, and inheritance strategies
  - Write repository interfaces (CRUD, query methods, @Query) and custom repository implementations
  - Understand implications of FetchType.EAGER vs LAZY and N+1 query problems and mitigation strategies
  - Apply pagination and sorting in repositories and expose them via APIs
- Understand ORM and JPA behavior in depth:
  - Entity lifecycle states (transient, persistent, detached, removed)
  - Persistence context, first-level cache, and how it interacts with transactions
  - Dirty checking, flushing behavior, and impact on performance
  - Batch updates and inserts, statement caching, and JDBC-level optimizations
- Design transactional boundaries correctly:
  - Use @Transactional semantics (propagation, isolation, readOnly) and understand their impact
  - Manage nested transactions, rollbacks, and checked/unchecked exceptions
  - Recognize common pitfalls (transactional on private methods, self-invocation, proxies)
- Work with multiple data sources if required:
  - Configure multiple DataSource beans and transaction managers
  - Route repositories to different data sources, manage cross-DB transactions where feasible
- Integrate alternative persistence technologies when appropriate:
  - Spring Data JDBC, MongoDB, Redis, or other NoSQL stores and message stores
  - Criteria vs query methods vs specification pattern for complex queries
- Design schema and data models collaboratively with DB experts:
  - Reflect domain concepts in persistence models while avoiding anemic domain models
  - Plan migrations, versioning (Flyway, Liquibase), and rollback strategies
- Ensure data integrity and consistency:
  - Understand optimistic vs pessimistic locking and select the right strategy
  - Handle concurrency conflicts, stale data updates, and idempotent write operations","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Security with Spring Security","scope_included":"- Integrate and configure Spring Security in Spring Boot applications:
  - Understand the security filter chain and how it is auto-configured in Spring Boot
  - Configure authentication, authorization, and custom access decision logic
- Implement authentication strategies:
  - Username/password with persistent user stores (DB, LDAP, external IdP)
  - JWT-based authentication and token validation
  - OAuth2/OIDC client and resource server behavior at an implementation level (not necessarily designing identity infrastructure)
- Implement fine-grained authorization:
  - URL-based vs method-level security (@PreAuthorize, @PostAuthorize, @Secured)
  - Role vs authority concepts and their mapping to business permissions
- Secure REST APIs:
  - CSRF considerations for stateless APIs, CORS configuration, and secure headers
  - Protect endpoints with scopes/claims/roles and manage security contexts
- Customize Spring Security:
  - Custom UserDetailsService, AuthenticationProvider, AuthenticationEntryPoint, access denied handlers
  - Customize login flows and error responses for APIs
- Understand common vulnerabilities and mitigations in Spring Boot contexts:
  - Injection attacks (SQL, JSON, header), XSS, CSRF, clickjacking, open redirects
  - Secure handling of secrets, tokens, and credentials (avoid hardcoding, use vaults/config server)
- Apply secure-by-default practices:
  - Limit exposure of Actuator endpoints and protect sensitive paths
  - Enforce HTTPS, HSTS, strict TLS versions, and strong cipher suites (in collaboration with DevOps)
  - Validate and sanitize external input systematically","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Integration, Messaging & Asynchronous Processing","scope_included":"- Consume and produce external HTTP services:
  - Use RestTemplate (legacy) and WebClient (reactive) with proper timeouts, connection pools, and error handling
  - Implement resilient calls with circuit breakers, retries, and bulkheads (using Spring Cloud CircuitBreaker, Resilience4j, or similar)
- Integrate with messaging systems:
  - Use Spring for Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, JMS, or other messaging abstractions
  - Configure producers, consumers, listener containers, concurrency, and error handling
  - Design message payloads, headers, and routing keys/topics for extensibility and backwards compatibility
- Implement asynchronous and scheduled tasks:
  - Use @Async, task executors, thread pool configuration, and understand impact on context propagation
  - Use @Scheduled and scheduling configuration for cron and fixed-rate/fixed-delay tasks
  - Ensure idempotency and error handling in async and scheduled jobs
- Use Spring Integration or Spring Cloud Stream where appropriate:
  - Understand channel-based and binder-based programming models at a practical level
  - Configure application bindings to various message brokers
- Understand eventual consistency patterns:
  - Apply outbox/inbox patterns or message deduplication in Spring Boot architectures
  - Handle at-least-once and at-most-once delivery semantics in design
- Document and manage integration contracts:
  - Maintain API and message contracts (payload structure, semantics)
  - Use contract testing frameworks or schema registries where adopted by the organization","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Architecture, Design & Microservices with Spring Boot","scope_included":"- Design Spring Boot applications following sound architectural principles:
  - Layered architecture (controller, service, repository, domain) and clear boundaries
  - Ports-and-adapters (hexagonal) or clean architecture using Spring beans and configuration
  - Recognize when to refactor from monolith to modular monolith or microservices
- Participate in microservices architecture using Spring Boot:
  - Understand service decomposition concerns and avoid over-fragmentation
  - Design service boundaries, APIs, and data ownership models
  - Handle cross-cutting concerns: security, logging, observability, configuration, error handling
- Use Spring Cloud components at a practical level where applicable:
  - Service discovery and registration (eureka, consul) as a consumer/implementer
  - External configuration management (Spring Cloud Config) for distributed environments
  - Client-side load balancing and fault tolerance libraries via Spring Cloud dependencies
- Make informed choices about inter-service communication:
  - REST vs messaging vs gRPC with Spring integration
  - Synchronous vs asynchronous communication and impact on coupling and resilience
- Apply DDD-inspired design in Spring Boot where appropriate:
  - Identify bounded contexts and aggregate roots and reflect them in Spring modules
  - Contain domain logic in domain services/entities instead of controllers
- Balance standards vs flexibility in large Spring Boot landscapes:
  - Standardize base configurations, common libraries, and internal starters
  - Allow exceptions when justified technically and documented
- Mentor others on architectural trade-offs in Spring Boot projects:
  - Evaluate cost vs benefit of introducing new Spring modules or 3rd party frameworks
  - Highlight operational impacts (observability, deployments, performance) of design decisions","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Performance, Scalability & Reliability in Spring Boot","scope_included":"- Diagnose and address performance issues in Spring Boot applications:
  - Analyze slow endpoints, heavy queries, and memory usage patterns
  - Use profiling tools and application metrics (via Actuator and external APM) to locate bottlenecks
- Optimize Spring Boot applications for throughput and latency:
  - Tune thread pools (web server, async executors, schedulers)
  - Tune database connections (connection pools, timeouts, pool sizes)
  - Configure HTTP server settings (max connections, keep-alive, compression) in coordination with ops teams
- Understand and mitigate common performance pitfalls in Spring/JPA:
  - N+1 queries, unnecessary eager fetching, misuse of cascades
  - Inefficient serialization, excessive object creation, large response payloads
- Design for scalability:
  - Stateless services where feasible to enable horizontal scaling
  - Externalize session state when sessions are needed (Redis or similar)
  - Partition workloads across instances, use backpressure strategies with reactive or messaging-based designs
- Improve reliability and resilience:
  - Implement robust retry, timeout, circuit breaker, and fallback patterns for remote calls
  - Use bulkheading and rate-limiting strategies to protect critical resources
  - Design graceful degradation behavior at the service and API level
- Manage resource usage:
  - Understand JVM memory settings and how they affect Spring Boot services
  - Monitor GC behavior and tune if necessary for long-running services
- Plan and implement performance testing strategies:
  - Collaborate on load, stress, and soak test design targeting Spring Boot endpoints
  - Interpret results to guide code or configuration changes","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Testing Strategy & Quality Practices in Spring Boot","scope_included":"- Implement comprehensive automated testing for Spring Boot applications:
  - Unit tests focusing on business logic without Spring context when possible
  - Slice tests for web, data, and other layers (@WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, etc.)
  - Integration tests using @SpringBootTest with realistic configurations
- Use Spring testing utilities effectively:
  - MockMvc for HTTP endpoint tests
  - TestEntityManager or transactional tests for persistence
  - TestRestTemplate or WebTestClient for full-stack endpoint testing
- Manage test data and environment:
  - Use in-memory databases or testcontainers for integration tests
  - Seed data via SQL scripts, builders, or factories while ensuring isolation and repeatability
- Apply mocking and stubbing appropriately:
  - Use mocking frameworks to isolate Spring beans in tests
  - Replace external integrations with stubs or mocks via profiles or configuration
- Introduce contract and integration testing for inter-service dependencies where relevant:
  - HTTP and messaging contract tests to reduce integration failures
- Integrate tests into CI/CD:
  - Ensure Spring Boot test suites are performant and provide quick feedback
  - Organize test suites (unit vs integration vs end-to-end) for pipeline stages
- Enforce quality gates:
  - Apply code coverage thresholds while focusing on meaningful coverage
  - Use static analysis and code quality tools integrated with Spring Boot codebases","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Observability, Monitoring & Actuator","scope_included":"- Use Spring Boot Actuator effectively:
  - Enable and configure health, metrics, info, env, and custom endpoints
  - Secure and limit access to sensitive endpoints
- Expose meaningful health and liveness/readiness information:
  - Implement custom HealthIndicators for dependencies (DB, messaging, external APIs)
  - Configure liveness/readiness probes for orchestrators (Kubernetes, etc.)
- Integrate metrics and tracing:
  - Use Micrometer to publish metrics to monitoring backends (Prometheus, Graphite, cloud-specific)
  - Instrument custom metrics for business and technical indicators
  - Integrate distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, Zipkin, Jaeger) with Spring Boot services
- Implement structured logging:
  - Configure logging frameworks (Logback, Log4j2) for JSON/structured logs
  - Use correlation IDs and MDC for request-level traceability
  - Log at appropriate levels, avoid sensitive data in logs
- Use observability data in operations and design decisions:
  - Interpret metrics, logs, and traces to identify bottlenecks and errors
  - Feed insights back into code, configuration, or architecture changes","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Cloud, Deployment & Runtime Environments","scope_included":"- Package and run Spring Boot applications in different environments:
  - Build executable JARs or WARs as required
  - Containerize Spring Boot apps using Docker with efficient images and layered jars
- Configure environment-specific behavior:
  - Use profiles and environment variables for dev/test/stage/prod
  - Externalize configuration using environment variables, config servers, or secret stores
- Understand deployment targets and integration points:
  - Run on application servers, standalone JVMs, or orchestrated platforms (Kubernetes, cloud PaaS)
  - Use health checks, probes, and startup/shutdown hooks in those environments
- Manage Spring Boot in cloud environments:
  - Understand cloud service integrations (databases, caches, message brokers) and corresponding Spring starters
  - Use cloud-specific Spring libraries (Spring Cloud AWS, GCP, Azure) where appropriate
- Ensure runtime robustness:
  - Configure logging, monitoring, and alerting hooks in production
  - Collaborate on rolling deployments, blue-green, or canary releases
- Handle configuration and secret management securely:
  - Integrate with secret managers or vaults
  - Avoid secrets in code, logs, or build artifacts
- Participate in incident response for Spring Boot services:
  - Use logs, metrics, and traces to triage and mitigate production issues
  - Contribute fixes and improvements to prevent recurrences","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Build, Dependency & Environment Management (Tooling)","scope_included":"- Manage builds for Spring Boot applications:
  - Configure Maven or Gradle for multi-module Spring Boot projects
  - Use Spring Boot plugins and packaging types correctly
  - Automate common tasks (tests, code quality checks, packaging, dockerization)
- Handle dependency management and versioning:
  - Use dependency management sections or BOMs to align versions
  - Resolve conflicts caused by transitive dependencies and understand implications for Spring Boot autoconfiguration
  - Plan and execute dependency upgrades with minimal disruption
- Configure IDEs and local environments for Spring Boot development:
  - Use IDE support for Spring (Spring Tools, IntelliJ Spring features) for navigation and refactoring
  - Set up local profiles, env variables, and run configurations
- Integrate with CI/CD pipelines:
  - Ensure builds, tests, and packaging steps run reliably in pipelines
  - Parameterize configuration for different pipeline stages and environments
- Use code quality and analysis tools with Spring Boot projects:
  - Static analysis, style checks, and security scanning
  - Dependency vulnerability scanning and remediation
- Automate repetitive tasks:
  - Create scripts or Gradle/Maven tasks for database migrations, test data setup, or verification steps
  - Standardize project templates and archetypes for new Spring Boot services","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Collaboration, Code Review & Technical Leadership in Spring Boot Projects","scope_included":"- Participate in and often lead technical discussions for Spring Boot-based systems:
  - Explain and defend design decisions using clear reasoning grounded in Spring capabilities and constraints
  - Identify risks and trade-offs in proposed solutions
- Perform high-quality code reviews on Spring Boot codebases:
  - Review for correctness, security, performance, readability, and adherence to architectural and Spring-specific guidelines
  - Catch common Spring-specific pitfalls (transactional misuse, bean scope issues, configuration anti-patterns)
- Mentor and guide less experienced developers:
  - Coach others on Spring Boot best practices, idioms, and patterns
  - Help teammates debug complex Spring issues and interpret framework behavior
- Collaborate across roles:
  - Work with architects, product owners, QA, and ops to design and evolve Spring Boot services
  - Communicate service capabilities and constraints clearly to non-Spring specialists
- Contribute to shared standards and libraries:
  - Help define and evolve internal Spring Boot guidelines, base projects, and shared modules
  - Encourage reuse and consistency across Spring Boot services
- Participate constructively in incident post-mortems:
  - Analyze root causes involving Spring Boot behavior or misconfiguration
  - Propose actionable improvements in code, tests, processes, or documentation","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Documentation, Governance & Knowledge Sharing","scope_included":"- Produce and maintain technical documentation for Spring Boot services:
  - Document APIs (OpenAPI/Swagger) and message contracts accurately
  - Document configuration options and environment-specific behavior
  - Describe architecture and component interactions at a service level
- Keep Spring Boot-related documentation aligned with implementation:
  - Update diagrams and docs when significant refactors occur
  - Capture known limitations, feature flags, and migration notes
- Contribute to organizational Spring Boot governance:
  - Adhere to and refine standards for security, logging, error handling, and testing
  - Propose deprecation and upgrade plans for outdated Spring Boot versions or modules
- Facilitate knowledge sharing:
  - Run or contribute to internal workshops, brown-bags, or onboarding sessions on Spring Boot topics
  - Share patterns and anti-patterns observed across projects
- Ensure compliance and auditability where required:
  - Help demonstrate how Spring Boot services meet security, logging, and regulatory requirements
  - Work with compliance teams to provide evidence from configuration, code, and runtime behavior","is_non_core_section":true}]}
